content: Ritonavir increases the levels of cabazitaxel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Co-administration should be avoided. Lopinavir and calcifediol interact by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially altering serum calcifediol levels and reducing its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustments of calcifediol may be necessary, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations should be closely monitored when initiating or discontinuing strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases cabozantinib levels through mechanisms involving other pathways, including MRP2 inhibition, which can enhance cabozantinib toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Ritonavir decreases canagliflozin levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and alternative antihyperglycemic agents should be considered in patients with renal impairment (e.g., CrCl <73 mL/min). Ritonavir and lopinavir increase cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. A reduction in cannabidiol dose may be necessary when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Lopinavir increases capmatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Plasma levels should be monitored during co-administration. Ritonavir increases cariprazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage modification details. Ritonavir increases carvedilol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cenobamate decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be required during co-administration. Similarly, cenobamate decreases ritonavir levels, necessitating therapy modification and monitoring. Ritonavir increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases cetirizine levels by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir increases chlordiazepoxide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and alternatives should be considered if available. Benzodiazepine doses may need to be lowered to reduce toxicity. Chloroquine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Lopinavir increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Co-administration with bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors should be avoided, as this may exacerbate bile salt accumulation in the liver, leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is necessary, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin. Ritonavir increases inhaled ciclesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Lopinavir increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome and QT interval prolongation. ECG monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Therapy should be modified, and alternatives should be considered if available. Ritonavir decreases clopidogrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing its bioactivation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir decreases codeine effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing its conversion to the active metabolite morphine. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Clotrimazole decreases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases topical cocaine levels by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Conivaptan increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases conjugated estrogens levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cortisone decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, ritonavir increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Crizotinib increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Ritonavir also increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. ECG monitoring is recommended. Crofeler increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Lopinavir increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid co-administration in patients with atrial fibrillation (CrCl <30 mL/min) or DVT/PE treatment (CrCl <50 mL/min). Dabrafenib decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Danazol increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Danicopan increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Dose reduction of P-gp substrates may be required to avoid adverse reactions. Darifenacin increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase darolutamide levels, as darolutamide is a P-gp and CYP3A4 substrate. Close monitoring for adverse reactions and dose adjustments are necessary. Darunavir and ritonavir increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Darunavir also increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dasatinib increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Ritonavir increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Caution and monitoring are advised. Deferasirox decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir decreases deferasirox levels through other mechanisms. Avoid potent UGT inducers with deferasirox. If co-administration is required, increase the initial deferasirox dose and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third when co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases desipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Lopinavir increases desvenlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised.
